newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian lek firms as currency flows dries up.
newsitem.headline: Albanian lek firms as currency flows dries up.

text.p: The Albanian lek strengthened against the dollar in Tirana's open-air currency market on Wednesday despite a nationwide state of emergency and tension in the south of the country.
"Business is down. A lot of people have no more leks to sell," said a dealer in the narrow streets outside the capital's main post office.
In the space of three hours over the morning the "grey" market rate -- dealers on the street are issued with licences -- firmed to 140 leks from 145.
Last week the lek briefly slumped to 160, a drop of 50 percent from the New Year, as Albanians dumped the currency fearing devaluation and hyper-inflation.
"When the lek dropped below 150 to the dollar, people simply could not afford to buy dollars any more," the dealer said.

The collapse of dubious pyramid investment schemes last month has taken Albania to the brink of economic crisis. Thousands of investors lost their life savings, triggering violent demonstrations across Europe's poorest country. The state bank fixed its dollar exchange rate at 142 leks on Wednesday.
